Report
rē-pōrt´
n. (an account given; reputation; rendering Hebrew shemuah, Greek akoē, marturia)
From Latin reportare, to carry back. In Scripture a report is either the gospel message carried to men, or a man's reputation carried among them.

Biblical Definition

Report in the Authorized Version means two things, and both matter. First, a message carried: Isaiah's great question, “Who hath believed our report? and to whom is the arm of the LORD revealed?” (Isa 53:1) — quoted by John and by Paul of the general unbelief that met the preaching of Christ, and answered in Romans 10 with the doctrine that faith cometh by hearing. Second, a man's standing among those who know him. The seven chosen to serve tables had to be “men of honest report, full of the Holy Ghost and wisdom” (Act 6:3) — character attested before gifts are deployed. An elder “must have a good report of them which are without; lest he fall into reproach and the snare of the devil” (1Ti 3:7) — the testimony of unbelieving neighbours counting as a qualification for office. And the whole company of the faithful is summed up in it: “For by it the elders obtained a good report” (Heb 11:2) — by faith, and the report they obtained was God's.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines report as an account returned, a statement of facts given in reply; rumor; and public character or reputation.

expand to see more

REPORT, v.t. To bear or bring back an answer, or to relate what has been discovered by a person sent to examine.

2. To give an account of; to relate; to tell.

3. To give an official account or statement.

REPORT, n. An account returned; a statement or relation of facts given in reply to inquiry.

2. Rumor; common fame; story circulated. 3. Repute; public character.

Key Scripture

Isa 53:1 — "Who hath believed our report? and to whom is the arm of the LORD revealed?"

Act 6:3 — "Wherefore, brethren, look ye out among you seven men of honest report, full of the Holy Ghost and wisdom, whom we may appoint over this business."

1Ti 3:7 — "Moreover he must have a good report of them which are without; lest he fall into reproach and the snare of the devil."

Heb 11:2 — "For by it the elders obtained a good report."

Modern Corruption

Reputation among outsiders has been dismissed as people-pleasing, but Paul made it an eldership qualification — while the report a church actually cultivates is too often platform rather than character.

expand to see more

Two failures run in opposite directions. The first shrugs off outside opinion entirely: what unbelievers think of a leader is held to be irrelevant, or even a badge of faithfulness when it is bad. 1 Timothy 3:7 forbids that shrug — a man must have a good report of them which are without, and Paul attaches a reason, lest he fall into reproach and the snare of the devil. The neighbours who watch a man pay his bills, treat his wife, and keep his word are competent witnesses to the things eldership requires.

The second failure cultivates the wrong report. Where a ministry is built on reach, the report that matters becomes visibility, and character verification is postponed until a scandal enforces it. Acts 6 puts the order the other way round for a job as ordinary as distributing food: honest report first, then appointment. And Hebrews 11 names the only report finally worth obtaining — it was obtained by faith, and the One giving it is not the crowd.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew shemuah (H8052), a thing heard, a report; Greek akoē (G189), the thing heard, and martureō (G3140), to bear witness — the message carried and the character attested.

expand to see more

Hebrew shemuah (H8052) — a report, tidings, thing heard; “who hath believed our report?” (Isa 53:1).

Greek akoē (G189) — hearing, the thing heard; John quotes Isaiah's report with this word (Joh 12:38), and Rom 10:17 makes faith come by it.

Greek martureō (G3140) — to bear witness, be well reported of; the honest report of Act 6:3 and the good report of Heb 11:2.

Usage

"“Who hath believed our report?” — the prophet's question about his own generation, and ours."

"“Men of honest report” — character verified before a table is served."

"“By it the elders obtained a good report” — and the One reporting is God."
